- Joint PRV + Pump
- Multi-objective RL
- Safe/Constrained RL
- Demand Uncertainty
- PDA/DDA
- Generalization
- Simulation-to-real
- EPANET + RL

اگر مقاله جدیدی Novelty پروژه را تهدید می‌کند، آن را برجسته کن.

اگر انتشار یک paper خیلی جدید است، تاریخ دقیق آن را مشخص کن.

==================================================
17. Evidence Quality
==================================================

برای یافته‌های مهم مشخص کن Evidence از کجاست:

- Proposal
- Seminar
- Local Corpus
- External Paper
- Review
- Thesis
- Dissertation
- Report
- Inference
- Hypothesis

همچنین depth را اعلام کن:

- Screening
- Targeted
- Deep

هیچ‌وقت:

- citation جعل نکن.
- title/author/year/DOI را حدس نزن.
- عدد بدون source نده.
- inference را fact معرفی نکن.
- recommendation را scientific truth معرفی نکن.

==================================================
18. Confidence
==================================================

برای یافته‌های مهم:

- High
- Medium
- Low

بده.

و علت confidence را توضیح بده.

برای Novelty محافظه‌کار باش.

==================================================
19. Proposal/Seminar Conflict Protocol
==================================================

اگر Proposal/Seminar با شواهد تعارض داشت:

1. Proposal/Seminar چه می‌گوید؟
2. Evidence چه می‌گوید؟
3. تعارض چیست؟
4. نوع مشکل:
   - wording
   - interpretation
   - implementation
   - methodological
   - experimental
   - fundamental scientific
5. شدت مشکل
6. Minimum Scientifically Valid Correction
7. آیا بدون تغییر Scope قابل اصلاح است؟
8. آیا تغییر Scope لازم است؟
9. آیا نیاز به تصمیم پژوهشگر/استاد دارد؟

اصل:

Scientific Validity
+
Maximum Preservation of Approved Scope
+
Minimum Necessary Correction

هیچ تعارضی را مخفی نکن.

==================================================
20. Scope Creep Prevention
==================================================

اگر ایده جذابی در ادبیات دیدی، صرفاً به خاطر جذابیتش پیشنهاد تغییر پروژه نده.

قبل از هر پیشنهاد توسعه بپرس:

- ضروری است؟
- مستقیماً به Research Question مربوط است؟
- در Scope می‌گنجد؟
- مشکل علمی فعلی را حل می‌کند؟
- Alternative ساده‌تری وجود دارد؟
- هزینه و ریسک آن چیست؟

هدف:

Maximum Scientific Quality
با
Minimum Unnecessary Complexity

==================================================
21. محدودیت‌های بررسی و Extraction
==================================================

اگر PDF یا منبعی به دلیل:

- OCR
- RTL
- جدول
- فرمول
- شکل
- نمودار
- scan
- extraction error

کامل قابل بررسی نبود:

آن را صریحاً گزارش کن.

به هیچ عنوان اطلاعات گمشده را حدس نزن.

اگر یک نتیجه مهم به اطلاعات یک جدول/شکل وابسته است و آن جدول/شکل قابل مشاهده نیست، آن نتیجه را به‌عنوان:

Pending Verification

علامت‌گذاری کن.

==================================================
22. خروجی نهایی
==================================================

گزارش نهایی دقیقاً با این ساختار ارائه شود:

# 1. Executive Summary

# 2. State of the Art

# 3. Research Corpus Overview

# 4. Literature Matrix

# 5. Closest Prior Works

# 6. What Has Already Been Done

# 7. What Appears to Be Missing

# 8. Proposal/Seminar Claims Review

# 9. Counter-Evidence

# 10. Novelty Assessment

# 11. PDA vs DDA Evidence

# 12. State Design Evidence

# 13. Action Design Evidence

# 14. Reward Design Evidence

# 15. PPO Assessment

# 16. Baseline Evidence

# 17. Demand Uncertainty Evidence

# 18. Network and Generalization Evidence

# 19. Evaluation Design Evidence

# 20. Major Methodological Risks

# 21. Decisions That Must Be Resolved Before Coding

# 22. Recommended Direction Within Approved Scope

# 23. Evidence Quality and Review Depth

# 24. Confidence and Limitations

برای هر recommendation مشخص کن:

- Evidence
- Reasoning
- Alternatives
- Risk
- Confidence

==================================================
23. Recommendation ≠ Decision
==================================================

در این Phase فقط Recommendation ارائه بده.

هنوز:

- Network انتخاب نکن.
- State نهایی نکن.
- Action نهایی نکن.
- Reward نهایی نکن.
- Baseline نهایی نکن.
- Methodology را تغییر نده.
- Scope را تغییر نده.

این تصمیم‌ها در Phaseهای بعدی بررسی خواهند شد.

==================================================
24. پایان Phase
==================================================

بعد از پایان Deep Literature Review:

- هیچ فایل پروژه را تغییر نده.
- هیچ کدی ایجاد یا اصلاح نکن.
- هیچ آزمایشی اجرا نکن.
- هیچ شبکه‌ای انتخاب نکن.
- هیچ State/Action/Reward را نهایی نکن.
- Proposal یا Seminar را تغییر نده.
- Scope را تغییر نده.
- هیچ project decision جدیدی ثبت نکن.

فقط گزارش نهایی را ارائه کن.

بعد از گزارش، متوقف شو و منتظر دستور بعدی من بمان.

هدف نهایی این Phase:

«تبدیل Proposal + Seminar + Research Corpus + ادبیات به‌روز به یک نقشه شواهد علمی عمیق، قابل ردیابی و قابل دفاع برای طراحی روش‌شناسی پروژه.»

اگر شواهد نشان دادند فرضی از من احتمالاً غلط است، واضح بگو.

اگر شواهد کافی نیست، واضح بگو.

اگر پژوهشی پیدا کردی که احتمالاً از چشم من یا پروژه دور مانده، برجسته کن.

اگر چیزی در extraction قابل اعتماد نیست، حدس نزن.

Scientific Integrity و Evidence همیشه بر سرعت، راحتی و توافق مقدم هستند.

‫دسته بندي پيشنهادي مقاﻻت‬
‫پس از انجام بررسيهاي پيشين، در گام نخست، ابعاد و ويژگيهاي كليدي مطالعات مورد تحليل مشخﺺ‬ ‫ميگردند.‬
‫پس از شناسايي اين ابعاد، ضروري است كه دستهبندي نظاممندي بر روي مقاﻻت اعمال شود. اين دستهبندي‬ ‫امكان مقايسه دقيق مطالعات را فراهم ميآورد و در نهايت، به شناسايي شكافهاي موجود در ادبيات پژوهش‬
‫‪(research gaps)‬منجر ميشود.‬
‫ابعاد به طور كل در ‪ ٩‬دسته بندي قرار گرفته و در ادامه شرح داده شده است.‬

‫هدف پژوهش‬ ‫اين بعد، هدف اصلي فني يا عملياتي مطالعه را مشخﺺ مينمايد.‬
‫‪ ‬مديريت نشت‬ ‫‪ o‬كاهش نشت‬ ‫‪ o‬ارزيابي نشت‬ ‫‪ o‬تشخيﺺ نشت‬ ‫‪ ‬كنترل و بهينهسازي فشار‬ ‫‪ ‬كاهش هزينههاي عملياتي‬ ‫‪ o‬كمينهسازي هزينه انرژي‬ ‫‪ ‬تابآوري و استحكام سيستم‬ ‫‪ o‬پاسخ به شكست لوله‬ ‫‪ o‬مديريت تغييرات تقاضا‬ ‫‪ ‬حفاظت از كيفيت آب (در داخل شبكه توزيع آب)‬ ‫‪ o‬كاهش آلودگي‬ ‫‪ o‬كنترل سن آب‬

‫حوزه كاربرد‬ ‫اين بعد، سيستم اصلي و دامنه عملياتي مطالعه را تعريف ميكند.‬
‫‪ ‬مديريت شبكه توزيع آب ‪(WDN)‬‬ ‫‪ o‬مديريت فشار‬ ‫‪ o‬مديريت نشت‬
‫‪ o‬كنترل عملياتي‬

‫نوع داده‬ ‫اين بعد، ماهيت دادههاي مورد استفاده براي مدلسازي و ارزيابي را توصيف‬
‫ميكند.‬ ‫‪ ‬دادههاي هيدروليكي شبيهسازيشده‬
‫‪ ‬دادههاي عملياتي واقعي‬ ‫‪ o‬دادههاي حسگر ‪SCADA‬‬
‫‪ ‬دادههاي مبتني بر رويداد‬ ‫‪ o‬الگوهاي تقاضا‬ ‫‪ o‬رويدادهاي شكست يا اختﻼل‬
‫‪٨٢‬‬

‫رويكرد شناختي‬ ‫اين بعد، رويكرد اصلي علمي يا محاسباتي بهكارگرفتهشده را‬
‫شناسايي ميكند.‬ ‫‪ ‬كنترل هوشمند‬ ‫‪ o‬يادگيري تقويتي ‪(RL)‬‬ ‫‪ ‬مبتني بر ارزش ‪Q-)‬‬ ‫‪(Learning, DQN, DDQN‬‬ ‫‪ ‬مبتني بر سياست ( ,‪PPO‬‬ ‫‪(TRPO, REINFORCE‬‬ ‫‪ ‬بازيگر-منتقد ( ,‪A٢C, DDPG‬‬ ‫‪(SAC, TD٣‬‬

 ‫‪ ‬يادگيري تقويتي چندعامل‬ ‫‪(MARL)‬‬
‫‪ o‬شبكههاي عصبي مصنوعي ‪(ANN)‬‬ ‫‪ o‬تكامل عصبي ‪(Neuro-Evolu on)‬‬
‫‪ ‬بهينهسازي متاهيوريستيك‬ ‫‪ o‬الگوريتم ژنتيك ‪(GA)‬‬ ‫‪ o‬بهينهسازي ازدحام ذرات ‪(PSO)‬‬
‫‪ o‬تكامل تفاضلي ‪(DE)‬‬ ‫‪ o‬بهينهسازي شاهين هريس ‪(HHO)‬‬
‫‪ ‬كنترل مبتني بر مدل‬ ‫‪ o‬كنترل مبتني بر قاعده‬ ‫‪ o‬كنترل مبتني بر بهينهسازي‬ ‫‪ ‬مدلسازي و شبيهسازي هيدروليكي (حمايتي)‬

‫محيط مﻄاﻟعه‬ ‫اين بعد، زمينه سيستم را كه مطالعه در آن انجام شده است، مشخﺺ مينمايد.‬
‫‪ ‬شبكه توزيع آب شبيهسازيشده‬ ‫‪ o‬شبكههاي معيار (مانند -‪Net٣, Anytown, D‬‬
‫‪(Town‬‬ ‫‪ o‬مدلهاي شبكه واقعي‬ ‫‪ ‬شبكه توزيع آب شهري عملياتي (موارد محدود)‬

‫متﻐيرهاي كنترل / تصميمگيري‬ ‫اين بعد، پارامترهاي عملياتي كه به طور فعال دستكاري ميشوند را‬
‫شناسايي ميكند.‬ ‫‪ ‬شيرهاي كاهش فشار ‪(PRVs)‬‬
‫‪ ‬پمﭗها‬ ‫‪ o‬وضعيت روشن/خاموش‬
‫‪ o‬كنترل سرعت متغير‬ ‫‪ ‬شيرهاي دروازهاي‬
‫‪ ‬متغيرهاي زمانبندي عملياتي‬

‫ويژگيهاي مسﺌله‬ ‫اين بعد، پيچيدگي ذاتي مسئله پژوهش را ترسيم ميكند.‬
‫‪ ‬رفتار ديناميك سيستم‬ ‫‪ ‬روابط هيدروليكي ﻏيرخطي‬ ‫‪ ‬كنترل واقعيزمان يا نزديك به واقعيزمان‬
‫‪ ‬بهينهسازي چند هدفه‬ ‫‪ ‬فﻀاي حالت / عمل با ابعاد باﻻ‬ ‫‪ ‬عدم قطعيت سيستم و تغييرات تقاضا‬

‫تمركز ارزيابي عملكرد‬ ‫اين بعد، معيارهاي ارزيابي مورد استفاده را دستهبندي ميكند.‬
‫‪ ‬معيارهاي عملكرد هيدروليكي‬ ‫‪ ‬معيارهاي تلفات آب‬

‫بررسي شكاف هاي تحقيقاتي‬
‫مرور نظاممند ادبيات نشان ميدهد كه عليرﻏم پيشرفتهاي اخير در بهكارگيري يادگيري تقويتي عميق براي‬ ‫مديريت فشار در شبكههاي توزيع آب، هنوز فاصله معناداري ميان راهكارهاي پيشنهادي و الزامات بهرهبرداري‬ ‫واقعي از اين سامانههاي زيرساختي وجود دارد. اين فاصله، ناشي از مجموعهاي از شكافهاي تحقيقاتي ساختاري‬
‫است كه ضرورت توسعه رويكردهاي كنترلي پايدارتر، تطبيقيتر و قابلاعتمادتر را برجسته ميسازد.‬
‫نخستين شكاف اساسي، وابستگي شديد روشهاي كنترلي متداول و حتي برخي رويكردهاي يادگيريمحور به‬ ‫مدلهاي دقيق هيدروليكي است. روشهاي بهينهسازي كﻼسيك و كنترل پيشبين، عملكرد خود را بر پايه يك‬ ‫مدل از پيش كاليبرهشده بنا ميكنند؛ مدلي كه در عمل بهدليل تغييرات مستمر در شرايط بهرهبرداري، الگوهاي‬ ‫مصرف و فرسودگي زيرساخت، بهسرعت اعتبار خود را از دست ميدهد. اگرچه يادگيري تقويتي عميق بهعنوان‬ ‫يك چارچوب بدون مدل معرفي شده است، اما بسياري از مطالعات اوليه در اين حوزه همچنان به ساختارهايي‬ ‫متكي هستند كه بهطور ﻏيرمستقيم از فروض مدلمحور تأثير ميپذيرند يا نسبت به خطاهاي مدل حساس باقي‬ ‫ميمانند. اين مسئله نشان ميدهد كه نياز به الگوريتمي با پايداري ذاتي در فرآيند يادگيري و مقاومت در برابر‬
‫نوسانات محيطي همچنان برطرف نشده است.‬
‫دومين شكاف مهم، ناپايداري فرآيند آموزش در بسياري از الگوريتمهاي ‪ DRL‬مورد استفاده براي كنترل فشار‬ ‫است. شبكههاي توزيع آب، سامانههايي ايمنيمحور محسوب ميشوند كه در آنها تغييرات ناگهاني يا افراطي در‬
‫تنظيمات شيرهاي فشارشكن ميتواند به بروز شرايط بحراني منجر شود. با اين حال، برخي الگوريتمهاي رايج‬ ‫مانند ‪ DDPG‬يا روشهاي مبتني بر ارزش، به نوسانات شديد در سياست كنترلي، حساسيت به تنظيم‬
‫ابرپارامترها و واگرايي در فرآيند يادگيري دچار هستند. اين ناپايداريها مانعي جدي براي اعتمادپذيري و قابليت‬ ‫استقرار اين روشها در كاربردهاي واقعي ايجاد ميكند.‬
‫در اين زمينه، الگوريتم ‪ (Proximal Policy Op miza on (PPO‬بهطور مستقيم اين شكاف را هدف قرار‬ ‫ميدهد. سازوكار بهروزرساني سياست در ‪ ،PPO‬كه بر پايه تابع هدف جانشينِ بريدهشده ( ‪Clipped‬‬
‫‪ (Surrogate Objec ve‬بنا شده است، بهصورت صريح از اعمال تغييرات بزرگ و ناگهاني در سياست‬ ‫جلوگيري ميكند. اين ويژگي موجب ميشود فرآيند يادگيري بهصورت تدريجي، پايدار و قابلكنترل انجام شود؛‬
‫خصوصيتي كه براي كنترل بﻼدرنگ شيرهاي فشارشكن در شبكههاي واقعي حياتي است.‬
‫سومين شكاف كليدي، عدم كارايي بسياري از الگوريتمهاي موجود در مواجهه با فﻀاي عمل پيوسته و چندبعدي‬ ‫است. مديريت همزمان چندين ‪ PRV‬ذاتاً يك مسئله با فﻀاي عمل پيوسته و وابستگيهاي متقابل ميان‬
‫‪٨٤‬‬

 ‫عملگرهاست. روشهاي مبتني بر فﻀاي عمل گسسته، نظير ‪ ،DQN‬براي چنين مسئلهاي نيازمند‬ ‫سادهسازيهاي شديد هستند كه منجر به كاهش دقت كنترلي و افزايش بار محاسباتي ميشود. در مقابل، ‪PPO‬‬

Water Pressure Optimisation for Leakage Management Using Deep
Reinforcement Learning
By Ahmed Mohamed Abdelkader Atia Negm
In collaboration with Designed Network Solutions Ltd.
This thesis is submitted to Lancaster University for the Degree of Doctor of Philosophy
January 2024
This project was supported by the Centre for Global Eco-Innovation and is part financed by the European Regional Development Fund.

 ‫بسم الله الرحمان الرحيم‬
In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
I

 Abstract
In this thesis, we introduce a novel approach to pressure management using deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithms. Exploiting DRL algorithms to optimise pressure management in water distribution networks (WDNs) provides a more computationally efficient and resilient method to reduce background and burst leakage. Using DRL to manage pressure has proven as a valuable method to reduce leakage and carbon emissions in two case studies based on a real and benchmark water network. A cohort of eight DRL algorithms of varying natures are implemented on a benchmark test network and real network model of varying sizes to prove their scalability. An investigation on their ability to reduce both background and burst leakage is conducted to highlight their abilities with regards to different leak sizes.
The application of deep reinforcement learning algorithms to control leakage in WDNs builds on from two extensive reviews of leakage management and DRL applications in the urban water systems. Collating this literature pinpoints the novelty in applying deep reinforcement learning algorithms to control pressure in WDNs and provides context to the thesis. To develop DRL algorithms fit for WDN operations, a novel python-based environment is created that can communicate the hydraulic capabilities of EPANET to the DRL agent. This involved multiple design choices including action space and observation space selection as well as formulating a reward function suitable for the multiple objectives relating to leakage reduction.
Regarding background leakage, the best performing DRL algorithm resulted in 65.2% reduction in leakage in the benchmark network. However, the investigation on the real water network provided by Northumbrian Water Living has proved the strong dependency between valve locations and pressure management hence resulting in a negligible background leakage reduction. The ability of the DRL algorithms to deal with uncertainty through randomised burst nodes was investigated in the second case study. DRL policies demonstrated resilience in comparison to the standard optimisation algorithms used (differential evolution, particle swarm optimisation, and nelder mead). The best performing DRL algorithm predicted a 58.46% leakage reduction and 5650kg of reduced CO2 emissions in the benchmark water network. On the other hand, the best DRL performance optimised the real water network by reducing the leakage by 5.79% and c

Leveraging Deep Reinforcement Learning for Water Distribution Systems with Large Action Spaces and
Uncertainties: DRL-EPANET for Pressure Control
Anas Belfadil1; David Modesto, Ph.D.2; Jordi Meseguer, Ph.D.3; Bernat Joseph-Duran, Ph.D.4; David Saporta5; and Jose Antonio Martin Hernandez, Ph.D.6

Abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has undergone a revolution in recent years, enabling researchers to tackle a variety of previously inaccessible sequential decision problems. However, its application to the control of water distribution systems (WDS) remains limited. This research demonstrates the successful application of DRL for pressure control in WDS by simulating an environment using EPANET version 2.2, a popular open-source hydraulic simulator. We highlight the ability of DRL-EPANET to handle large action spaces, with more than 1 million possible actions in each time step, and its capacity to deal with uncertainties such as random pipe breaks. We employ the Branching Dueling Q-Network (BDQ) algorithm, which can learn in this context, and enhance it with an algorithmic modification called BDQ with fixed actions (BDQF) that achieves better rewards, especially when manipulated actions are sparse. The proposed methodology was validated using the hydraulic models of 10 real WDS, one of which integrated transmission and distribution systems operated by Hidralia, and the rest of which were operated by Aigües de Barcelona. DOI: 10.1061/JWRMD5.WRENG-6108. © 2023 American Society of Civil Engineers.
Practical Applications: This research presents the DRL-EPANET framework, which combines deep reinforcement learning and EPANET to optimize water distribution systems. Although the focus of this paper is on pressure control, the approach is highly versatile and can be applied to various sequential decision-making problems within WDS, such as pump optimization, energy management, and water quality control. DRL-EPANET was tested and proven effective on 10 real-world WDS, resulting in as much as 26% improvement in mean pressure compared with the reference solutions. The framework offers real-time control solutions, enabling water utility operators to react quickly to changes in the network. Additionally, it is capable of handling stochastic scenarios, such as random pipe bursts, demand uncertainty, contamination, and component failures, making it a valuable tool for managing complex and unpredictable situations. This method can be developed more with the use of model-based deep reinforcement learning for enhanced sample efficiency,

Multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for real-time scheduling of pump and valve in water distribution networks
Shiyuan Hu, Jinliang Gao * and Dan Zhong
School of Environment, Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin, China *Corresponding author. E-mail: gjl@hit.edu.com
JG, 0000-0002-6662-0187

ABSTRACT
With energy and water resources shortages, the energy and water resources managements of water distribution networks (WDNs) have become increasingly important. However, achieving real-time scheduling of pump and valve in dynamic environments remains challenging. Thus, this study proposes a multi-agent reinforcement learning scheduling framework to address the uncertainty of water demand in WDNs. First, we constructed a WDN environment and modelled the scheduling problem as a Markov decision process. Second, a multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) method was used to determine the strategy of the fully cooperative multi-agent task. Moreover, the impacts of energy and water loss costs on the scheduling strategy were explored. Finally, the results were compared with those of a genetic algorithm (GA), particle swarm optimisation (PSO), and differential evolution (DE) to verify the performance and robustness of the proposed model. The results show that water loss dominates the scheduling process, and the scheduling solutions for minimising water loss and energy costs are mainly affected by the demand pattern of consumers rather than the energy tariff. The proposed MADDPG model outperforms the GA, PSO, and DE models, achieving a signiﬁcantly faster solution, which is advantageous for practical applications.
Key words: energy cost, multi-agent reinforcement learning, pump and valve, real-time schedule, water distribution network, water loss cost
HIGHLIGHTS
• A multi-agent reinforcement learning framework was constructed for real-time scheduling of pump and valve. • The scheduling problem of pump and valve was transformed into a Markov decision process. • Scheduling solutions for minimising water loss and energy costs are affected by the demand pattern of consumers rather than the energy
tariff.
• The MADDPG model can obtain a real-time solution that is superior to the GA, PSO, and DE in a relatively short time.

1556:Augmented Random Search (ARS) ARS is a model-free DRL algorithm that utilises a simple random search algorithms with a few augmentations on the parameterised policy equation. This was first introduced in (Mania, Guy and Recht, 2018) where the authors attempted to improve sample efficiency in DRL models by developing a method that harnesses simple random search. ARS was aimed to present the simplest model-free method that can tackle current continuous control benchmarks in a more sample efficient manner than (Salimans et al., 2017)’s evolution strategy (ES). Several policies are created through random perturbations that are ranked depending on their performance. The policy is updated based on the reward-weight sum of these perturbations. The adaptive step size controls the magnitude of these policy updates effectively tackling the explorationexploitation dilemma. This process is repeated until the algorithm converges to the best achievable policy. Results from the initial experiment show an improvement in sample efficiency greater than 15 times than the best competing model-free methods and performed routinely higher than standard PPO, A2C, and TRPO algorithms (Mania, Guy and Recht, 2018). However, the ARS performance is plagued with high variance which suggests that the
2351: implementation time and the lower computational load, DRL algorithms provide a true promise for real-time control (less than 0.4s per prediction) on a DMA level. However, due to the complexity of whole water distribution systems shown in SZ08, real-time control is slightly out of the scope of DRL using regular processors (around 10s per prediction). Using high end computing could improve that greatly and make real-time control of whole system zones a reality. The use of real-time control in WDN pressure management is a novelty that is bound to increase water savings and carbon reductions as they allow valves to react more instantly to changes in the network whereas the current standard receives signals hourly or even daily. Comparing the two case studies, it is clear that the optimisation approach is more beneficial on a DMA scale however still applicable on a large scale. The SZ08 case study provides a more complex large-scale problem with multiple demand patterns and varying topographies. Therefore, DRL algorithms that prioritise stability and sample efficiency such as TRPO perform better. On the other hand, Jowitt & Xu provides a smaller scale and better valve locations resulting in better overall results. DRL algorithms with better exploration properties managed to overcome local optima found at 780-800 with high water saved% and high-pressure violations. Thus, hybrid methods such as A2C and SAC performed well whilst the distributional DRL method TQC performed best. The difference in performance between the two case studies could suggest that optimising on a DMA scale could affect neighbouring areas resulting in additional trade-offs. DRL models can be trained to enact pressure control policies that significantly minimise water loss on the DMA level nevertheless future work should focus on experimenting with multi-agent DRL control. Using this technology, it may be possible to train agents individually on DMAs and have them communicate through an overarching MADRL system. Hence, this ensures that we harness the possible savings on a DMA level without creating sub-optimal states on neighbouring DMAs in a more open-looped fashion. The design of DRL algorithms is very complex and is brim with possibilities for customisation hence future work should encourage the use of different neural network architectures, optimisers, activation functions and pre-training techniques.
2930:Hybrid models include A2C, DDPG and SAC. Plagued by its sensitivity to non-stationary environments, DDPG could not perform at the same level as the other DRL algorithms resulting in 18.54 average episodic reward which was marginally better than the benchmark PSO algorithm. DDPG’s slow adaptation of the target networks and deterministic policy gradients making it unsuitable for the burst scenario. Surprisingly, SAC’s incorporation of an entropy term to encourage exploration did not wage as well as expected in the burst scenario leading to an episodic reward of 21.82. The best explanation to this could be a misleading critic neural network as the value function fails to include the stochasticity necessary to judge the actor due to the changing environment. This would also explain how using and advantage function in the A2C algorithm greatly improves the results reaching the best overall performance with an episodic reward of 42.15. The advantage function provides a measure of how good an action is in comparison to the average action for a given state providing more efficient exploration and a clearer credit assignment. A2C achieves this high reward by striking the best compromise between leakage reduction (58.46%) and minimising pressure violations (67) therefore improving on both ARS and Recurrent PPO’s performances.
3061:Performance Using the results presented in figures 6-8 & 6-9 and the key results in table 6-3, we discuss the performances of the algorithms tested. The reward function used to evaluate the models was altered to better suit the SZ08 network in equation 6-1. The performance of the algorithms varied greatly with some unable to optimise the test case due to its complexity. The results table showed how the best algorithms were the ones that focused on balancing the two objectives rather than minimising leakage which resulted in negative rewards. A closer look on figure 6-9 shows the temporal rewards during the 72 timesteps of the tests. This line graph highlighted a clear pattern of higher rewards during lower customer demand times of the day. However, due to the complexity of whole water distribution systems shown in SZ08, real-time control is slightly out of the scope of DRL using regular processors (around 10s per prediction). Using high end computing could improve that greatly and make real-time control of whole system zones a reality. The use of real-time control in WDN pressure management is a novelty that is bound to increase water savings and carbon reductions as they allow valves to react more instantly to changes in the network whereas the current standard receives signals hourly or even daily. Comparing the two case studies, it is clear that the optimisation approach is more beneficial on a DMA scale however still applicable on a large scale. The SZ08 case study provides a more complex large-scale problem with multiple demand patterns and varying topographies. Therefore, DRL algorithms that prioritise stability and sample efficiency such as TRPO perform better. On the other hand, Jowitt & Xu provides a smaller scale and better valve locations resulting in better overall results. DRL algorithms with better exploration properties managed to overcome local optima found at 780-800 with high water saved% and high-pressure violations. Thus, hybrid methods such as A2C and SAC performed well whilst the distributional DRL method TQC performed best. The difference in performance between the two case studies could suggest that optimising on a DMA scale could affect neighbouring areas resulting in additional trade-offs. DRL models can be trained to enact pressure control policies that significantly minimise water loss on the DMA level nevertheless future work should focus on experimenting with multi-agent DRL control. Using this technology, it may be possible to train agents individually on DMAs and have them communicate through an overarching MADRL system. Hence, this ensures that we harness the possible savings on a DMA level without creating sub-optimal states on neighbouring DMAs in a more open-looped fashion. The design of DRL algorithms is very complex and is brim with possibilities for customisation hence future work should encourage the use of different neural network architectures, optimisers, activation functions and pre-training techniques.

DDPG’s slow adaptation of the target networks and deterministic policy gradients making it unsuitable for the burst scenario. ABSTRACT
The efficient and sustainable supply and transport of water is a key component to any functioning civilisation making the role of urban water systems (UWS) inherently crucial to the wellbeing of its customers. However, managing water is not a simple task. Whether it is ageing infrastructure, transient flows, air cavities or low pressures; water can be lost as a result of many issues that face UWSs. The complexity of those networks grows with the high urbanisation trends and climate change making water companies and regulatory bodies in need of new solutions. So, it comes as no surprise that many researchers are invested in innovating within the water industry to ensure that the future of our water is safe.
Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has the potential to tackle complexities that used to be very challenging as it relies on deep neural networks for function approximation and representation. This technology has conquered many fields due to its impressive results and can effectively revolutionise UWS. In this article, we explain the background of DRL and the milestones of this field using a novel taxonomy of the DRL algorithms. This will be followed by with a novel review of DRL applications in the UWS which focus on water distribution networks and stormwater systems. The review will be concluded with critical insights on how DRL can benefit different aspects of urban water systems.

Article
Real-Time Scheduling of Pumps in Water Distribution Systems Based on Exploration-Enhanced Deep Reinforcement Learning
Shiyuan Hu 1, Jinliang Gao 1,* , Dan Zhong 1, Rui Wu 2 and Luming Liu 3

1 School of Environment, Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin 150090, China 2 Guangdong Yuehai Water Investment Co., Ltd., Shenzhen 518021, China 3 National Engineering Research Center of Urban Water Resources Co., Ltd., Harbin Institute of Technology,
Harbin 150090, China
* Correspondence: gjl@hit.edu.cn

Abstract: Effective ways to optimise real-time pump scheduling to maximise energy efﬁciency are being sought to meet the challenges in the energy market. However, the considerable number of evaluations of popular optimisation methods based on metaheuristics cause signiﬁcant delays for real-time pump scheduling, and the simpliﬁcation of traditional deterministic methods may introduce bias towards the optimal solutions. To address these limitations, an exploration-enhanced deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework is proposed to address real-time pump scheduling problems in water distribution systems. The experimental results indicate that E-PPO can learn suboptimal scheduling policies for various demand distributions and can control the application time to 0.42 s by transferring the online computation-intensive optimisation task ofﬂine. Furthermore, a form of penalty of the tank level was found that can reduce energy costs by up to 11.14% without sacriﬁcing the water level in the long term. Following the DRL framework, the proposed method makes it possible to schedule pumps in a more agile way as a timely response to changing water demand while still controlling the energy cost and level of tanks.

All 4 records from the result set are below. Note: abstracts are present for every entry, but rather than reproducing them in full I've summarized each and kept any exact wording to short quoted fragments.

---

**1. "A Smart Water Distribution Network Management Framework Based on Internet of Things and Reinforcement Learning Technologies"**
- Year: 2026
- Venue: Journal of Soft Computing and Data Mining
- First author: Ibraheem A Aidan
- Abstract (summary): Presents a hybrid IoT–reinforcement learning architecture joining live sensing, data synchronization, adaptive control, and prediction. Distributed nodes gather pressure, flow, and energy readings, relayed over MQTT into a time-series database for feature extraction and anomaly detection, while a PPO agent learns policies to cut leakage and energy use without sacrificing hydraulic stability. Testing used EPANET 2.2 with the C-Town benchmark under 24-hour diurnal demand, comparing threshold-based SCADA (Model A), a "hybrid PID-Model Predictive Control (PID-MPC) controller (Model C)", and the proposed IoT-RL scheme (Model B). Reported gains for Model B: latency down 93.3% and accuracy up 22.7% versus Model A, 12.2% accuracy gain over Model C, and ~95% higher throughput; figures were generated in MATLAB from EPANET-based scripts.

**2. "Energy-Efficient Joint Scheduling of Pumps and Valves in Water Distribution Network Using Hybrid Optimization Algorithm"**
- Year: 2023
- Venue: Environmental Claims Journal
- First author: Waghmare Shwetambari Pandurang
- Abstract (summary): Argues that utilities have historically treated "pumping efficiency and pressure control" as separate concerns. Since modern pumps often carry variable speed drives, outlet pressure can be regulated via speed, and inlet pressure at a pressure-reducing valve can be lowered by altering upstream pumping when no intermediate tank exists; pressure-dependent leakage should also inform schedules. The work optimizes on/off switching timetables for pumps and valves in large-scale networks to minimize energy cost while satisfying nodal demand and reducing head loss, models shaft power via quadratic polynomial fitting, and examines variable speed pumps for pressure reliability, leakage, and power draw. A "hybrid binary dragonfly-enhanced Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm" is evaluated under three tariffs in MATLAB with the EPANET toolkit across varying horizons and network changes.

**3. "WaterAdmin: Orchestrating Community Water Distribution Optimization via AI Agents"**
- Year: 2026
- Venue: arXiv.org
- First author: Jiaqi Wen
- Abstract (summary): Addresses scheduling of pumps and valves in community water systems to satisfy demand at minimal energy cost. Conventional optimization assumes well-modeled conditions, yet real communities face shifting factors like human activity and weather that reshape demand and zone-level targets faster than such methods can absorb. LLM agents parse heterogeneous context well but "are not suitable for directly producing reliable real-time control actions." The proposed bi-level design pairs upper-level LLM context abstraction with lower-level optimization-based control, implemented on EPANET, yielding better pressure reliability and lower energy use in dynamic settings.

**4. "Multi-algorithm reinforcement learning framework with feedforward networks for resilient water tank scheduling systems"**
- Year: 2026
- Venue: Complex & Intelligent Systems
- First author: Hee-beom Park
- Abstract (summary): Benchmarks PPO, DQN, and A3C for water tank scheduling over multi-day horizons, with simulated demand variability, extreme scenarios, and LSTM-based temporal modeling. === LIEMBERGER ===
This paper provides a long overdue update on the global non-revenue water (NRW) estimates, initially published in a World Bank publication (Kingdom et al., 2006) more than 10 years ago. The authors use a similar approach based on latest data to estimate volumes of water lost by water utilities around the world. The conclusion of this study is that the 2006 estimates were extremely conservative and that realistic NRW estimates are significantly higher. The global volume of NRW has been estimated to be 346 million cubic meters per day or 126 billion cubic meters per year. Conservatively valued with only USD 0.31 per cubic meter, the cost/value of water lost amounts to USD 39 billion per year. Not only is this an enormous financial concern, elevated NRW detracts from water utilities, in a time of increasing scarcity and climate change, from reaching their goals of full service coverage, at a reliable level of service at an affordable price.
The global volume of NRW has been calculated to be 346 million cubic meters per day or 126 billion cubic meters per year. To put this in some perspective, this annual volume is about 70% of the average flow of the Niger River – the principal River in West Africa, and nearly 50% of the average flow of the Ganges River in India. But more importantly, the aggregate NRW is 30% of water system input volumes across the world.
billion m3/year
billion USD/year
The new model has now been used to run a simulation with 2005 data to compare the result with World Bank publication (Kingdom et al., 2006) which used 2005 data. The result shows a significant difference which can be explained by the conservative assumptions made in 2006 and the fact that the first model used the supplied urban population only while this model does not differentiate between urban and rural and includes all piped water supply systems. The difference to the model published by the Asian Development Bank (Liemberger and Frauendorfer, 2010) has similar reasons.

=== ABDY SAYYED 2015 PDA (abstract) ===
Abstract EPANET 2 has been used previously to simulate pressure-deficient operating conditions in water distribution systems by: (a) executing the algorithm repetitively until convergence is achieved; (b) modifying the source code to cater for pressure-dependent outflows; or (c) incorporating artificial elements e.g., reservoirs in the data input file. This paper describes a modelling approach that enables operating conditions with insufficient pressure to be simulated in a single execution of EPANET 2 without modifying the source code. This is achieved by connecting a check valve, a flow control valve and an emitter to the demand nodes. Thus the modelling approach proposed enhances an earlier formulation by obviating the need for an artificial reservoir at the nodes with insufficient pressure. Also, we removed a previous limitation in the modelling of pressure-dependent nodal flows to better reflect the performance of the nodes with insufficient flow and pressure. input.description: Extract Negm thesis limitations and assumptions

content.content:
=== NEGM LIMITATIONS / ASSUMPTIONS ===
7. Conclusions
In the process of advancing leakage management in water distribution network, this research has narrowed down to a focus on prevention through pressure management. Through proper valve control, WDN can simultaneously minimise leakage in the network without violating OFWAT regulated pressure limits. A novel methodology the exploits the capabilities of DRL algorithms for WDN applications has been developed to tackle background and burst leakage. A cohort of eight DRL algorithms and three benchmark optimisation algorithms are implemented to case studies consisting of four experiments in total applied to two different networks. In this chapter, the overall conclusions of the research are drawn from the case studies and their results. Any assumptions made during the research are elicited followed by the limitations. Finally, recommendations for future research are proposed to aid with the development of the research further.
Chapter 2
Prior to developing the DRL algorithms or the environment, a literature set was produced to explain the necessity of leakage management in WDNs, and current practices tackle this problem The main conclusions underscore the importance of diverse leakage assessment strategies including the Top-down, MNF analysis, and BABE methods, while advocating for a combination of methodologies for a more comprehensive assessment. Leakage detection involves inspection robotic platforms and non-intrusive hardware methods. However, advances in software methods such as data-driven leakage detection, especially in hybrid approaches with neural networks, show promise. Effective leakage control encompasses pressure management and asset management considering various impact factors. Considering pressure management requires emphasis on optimal valve placement and control. In this research, the path of leakage reduction through pressure management is explored further through the novel introduction of DRL algorithms for valve control.
Chapter 3
Hereby, a review on the application of DRL in all aspects of urban water systems was conducted to validify the novelty. In this section a comprehensive review of DRL methods coupled with a classification tree leads the path to DRL in UWS. This is followed by a review of current research and trends of DRL in different aspects of UWS. The main conclusions of this literature set highlight the impact of the use of deep neural networks for function approximation leading to improved scalability and resulted in many successes across simulated and real applications. Current DRL trends tackle high dimensional complexity by mimicking
173

 human psychology and natural hierarchy structures. A novel classification tree was established to help new researchers navigate better. The application of DRL in the UWS is still developing yet it shows great promise to improve our current practices with water. Early efforts to benchmark DRL test beds and environments will aid the growth of this topic. Challenges of applying DRL to water systems include testing and validation through real life models.
Chapter 4
The aim to deploy deep reinforcement learning methods for the optimisation of pressure management in WDNs could not be realised without the RL environment. As the literature suggests, building the DRL environment was an integral part of the research as it dictates the interactions between the agent and the WDN. The environment used managed to depict the problem effectively and lead the agents towards optimisation. All the necessary sections required to establish the environment were covered in chapter 4. The conclusions drawn from this chapter were crucial to the development of the research and highlight important remarks for the implementation of DRL in WDNs. Creating the environment has allowed for the use of both DRL and non-DRL methods to optimise the WDN models while leveraging the hydraulic simulation capabilities of EPANET. Implementing environment design for real networks will require the hydraulic solver capabilities of EPANET or a similar hydraulic solver. Input files developed from utility data platforms can be used in the environment as shown in the SZ08 network.

content.content:
• Hydraulic models used are considered the digital twin of the real networks. When implemented on the water network, the DRL algorithms will be acting based on real data making it less susceptible to discrepancies in the model. For the purposes of this study, a real-life implementation was not possible as there are no test networks available in the UK. The first test network will be built by Northumbrian Water and expected to be ready by 2025.
• Carbon emissions conversion factors were used from the government publication for 2023 (Department for Energy Security and Net Zero, 2023). The assumption made is that all the relevant carbon emissions are a result of leakage where in practice minimising leakage effects pumping and other network properties that might decrease carbon emissions further. For the scope of this study, only the direct carbon emissions are considered (scope 1).
• When selecting the action space, it was necessary to assume that it is continuous to allow the agents to roam the search space freely and equate the DRL agents to their benchmark alternatives. The assumption made was that pressure valves are able to process precise settings provided by the agent whereas in practice some control errors can be expected.
7.3. Recommendations for Future work
Beyond this research’s scope, there is room for development. In this thesis, we take the first steps in deploying deep reinforcement learning for leakage reduction in water distribution networks yet the path to a fully realised system requires further work. To conclude this research, we recommend future research to include the following.
As this field continues to grow, so does the need to benchmark case studies and environments. Therefore, it would be beneficial to collate and benchmark the DRL environments created to solve certain problems withing UWSs. For example, the environment created for this research can prove as a useful benchmark to train DRL agents for leakage prevention or (Hajgató, Paál and Gyires-Tóth, 2020)’s environment for pump control. It is important to intensify DRL research in leakage management applications. The management of in pipe inspection robots can be controlled through DRL algorithms or even a prediction agent can be trained to classify leaks and leak locations. These are a few examples regarding the possibilities of DRL in leakage management. From an engineering perspective, it is crucial that researchers exploring this topic confirm the validity of the application through live data or ground truth models. To achieve that, DRL algorithms should be built with reliability and scalability in mind.
179

 Different training methods such as Hindsight Experience Replay (HER), imitation learning and inverse RL should be investigated for their effectiveness in improving agent performances. These are among many tools that researchers should experiment with to further improve the results of DRL algorithms in mitigating leakage. Furthermore, researchers should aim to optimise neural networks through trialling different optimisers, activation functions, LSTM modules, architectures and more. It is proven the graph neural networks (GNNs) are effective in emulating the hydraulic behaviour of WDNs (Fan, Zhang and Yu, 2022) therefore it is safe to assume that they would be effective in creating DRL agents. There are many methods prevalent in the industrial application of DRL agents which could easily be repurposed for water distribution hence why researchers are encouraged to delve into DRL literature. It is adamant from the case studies that multi agent DRL could provide the resilience required to monitor DMAs separately and interactively ensuring that each network is optimised with an open loop between the DMAs. This method often incurs higher computational loads due to the complexities associated with multiple agents and the necessary environment modifications.
Incorporating other pressure influencing network elements such as pumps and air valves would add to the capabilities of the pressure control. The simplest way to achieve this is to add the new elements to the action space controlled by a single agent. This will require slight modifications to the environment to ensure that the different actuators can be managed simultaneously and account for the different nature of pumps to the pressure valves. Furthermore, variable speed pumps and fixed speed pumps constitute two different behaviours which should be considered

---

# گزارش Phase 1.5 — Deep Literature Review

**وضعیت Git (طبق §1):** شاخه `main`، ۲ کامیت. تنها تغییر working tree: `M .claude/skills/research-review/SKILL.md` — ۶۳۵ خط در working tree، **۰ بایت در HEAD**، sha256 `359c2685…`. هیچ فایل untracked نیست. **هیچ فایلی توسط من ایجاد، حذف یا ویرایش نشد.** هیچ dependency نصب نشد.

## ⚠️ سه تعارض/محدودیت که باید پیش از گزارش اعلام شوند

| # | مورد | وضعیت |
|---|---|---|
| **C-1** | CLAUDE.md §15 استفاده از **Subagents** را توصیه می‌کند؛ دستور سطح‌سشن می‌گوید «Do not call the AgentTool unless the user requested it». شما صریحاً درخواست نکردید. | محافظه‌کارانه **بدون Subagent** اجرا شد. تصمیم با شماست. |
| **C-2** | §6 و §21 دستور شما **بررسی بصری PDF** را می‌خواهند. `pdftoppm`/poppler-render، PyMuPDF، pypdf، pdfplumber، PIL، ImageMagick — **هیچ‌کدام نصب نیست**. | **غیرقابل‌اجرا.** نصب نکردم. همه شکل‌ها/جداول تصویری `Pending Verification` علامت خورده‌اند. |
| **C-3** | §16 دستور شما جست‌وجوی اکتشافی ۲۰۲۵–۲۰۲۶ را می‌خواهد. `WebSearch` خطا داد: `tool type 'web_search_20250305' is not supported for this model`. | **جایگزین یافتم:** Semantic Scholar API از طریق WebFetch. ۲ کوئری موفق (۷ مقاله جدید کشف شد)، سپس **HTTP 429 rate-limit**. پوشش خارجی **ناقص** است. |

---

# 1. Executive Summary

پروژه **در جهت علمی معتبری حرکت می‌کند**، اما **هر سه ادعای نوآوری Proposal، به‌درجات مختلف، توسط شواهد موجود در Corpus خودِ پروژه تضعیف می‌شوند.** ده یافته اصلی:

1. **تعارض داخلی جدی در Proposal.** بخش ۱ می‌گوید: «چارچوب منسجمی که PPO را با EPANET ادغام کند وجود ندارد». بخش ۲ و ضمیمه ۱ همان سند می‌گویند Negm (۲۰۲۴) دقیقاً یک محیط EPANET ساخته و PPO/SAC/TRPO/A2C را ارزیابی کرده. **این ادعا با سند خودش رد می‌شود.** (Confidence: High)

2. **نوآوری اول = «کارهای آینده» نزدیک‌ترین کار پیشین.** پایان‌نامه دکتری Negm (Lancaster, ۲۰۲۴) در §7.3 عیناً توصیه می‌کند: *"Incorporating other pressure influencing network elements such as pumps... The simplest way to achieve this is to add the new elements to the action space controlled by a single agent."* (Confidence: High)

3. **کنترل مشترک PRV+پمپ با DRL قبلاً انجام شده.** Hu, Gao & Zhong (۲۰۲۳، _Water Supply_ 23(7):2833) با **MADDPG**، **تحت عدم‌قطعیت تقاضا**، با **PDA + emitter**، پاداش چندهدفه (انرژی + تلفات آب) و baseline های GA/PSO/DE. (Confidence: High)

4. **PPO در نزدیک‌ترین کار پیشین برنده نشد.** در Negm ۲۰۲۴ روی سه مطالعه موردی: **TQC** بهترین روی Jowitt & Xu، **TRPO** بهترین روی شبکه واقعی SZ08، **A2C** بهترین در سناریوی burst (پاداش ۴۲.۱۵). PPO و Recurrent PPO میان‌رده. (Confidence: High)

5. **GA از PPO بهتر بود.** در Hu et al. (۲۰۲۳، _Systems_ 11(2):56): «GA converged after 100 epochs and were considered the **optimal solutions**»، سپس E-PPO، PPO، DE، PSO. نویسندگان خودشان E-PPO را «**suboptimal**» می‌نامند. مزیت DRL فقط **تأخیر استنتاج (۰.۴۲ ثانیه)** بود. (Confidence: High)

6. **شکاف تعمیم‌پذیری واقعی است — و قابل دفاع‌ترین نوآوری شماست.** Javed et al. (۲۰۲۵): *"Recurring gaps... include the lack of benchmark environments, **limited transferability across network topologies**, and minimal real-world implementations."* Hu et al. ۲۰۲۳: `generaliz` = **صفر**. Belfadil et al. ۲۰۲۳: `generaliz` = **صفر**. (Confidence: High)

7. **قوی‌ترین Counter-Evidence پروژه:** نتایج Negm روی benchmark (۶۵.۲٪ و ۵۸.۴۶٪ کاهش نشت) روی شبکه واقعی به **«negligible»** و **۵.۷۹٪** فروپاشید — به‌دلیل «strong dependency between valve locations and pressure management». **انتخاب شبکه، نتیجه را تعیین می‌کند.** (Confidence: High)

8. **Proposal مدل نشت را مشخص نکرده.** `emitter`=۰، `FAVAD`=۰، `leakage exponent`=۰، `N1`=۰، `PDA`/`DDA` عملاً غایب. اما هر سه کار نزدیک (Negm، Hu، Belfadil) **PDA** به‌کار برده‌اند و سمینار خودتان PDA را «راهبردی بسیار مهم» می‌نامد. **این شکاف مانع محاسبه «کاهش نشت» است.** (Confidence: High)

9. **آمار سرتیتر Proposal اشتباه و misattributed است.** «۳۲ میلیارد m³/سال (Guo et al., 2013)» — عدد منسوخ ۲۰۰۶ بانک جهانی، نسبت‌داده‌شده به مقاله‌ای درباره فیزیک ترک. منبع صحیح **در همین Corpus**: Liemberger & Wyatt → **۱۲۶ میلیارد m³/سال**، ۳۰٪ حجم ورودی، ۳۹ میلیارد دلار. (Confidence: High)

10. **فهرست منابع Proposal به‌طور سیستماتیک مخدوش است** (≥۱۴ ارجاع با venue/نویسنده/نهاد غلط، و placeholder «& colleagues»)، در حالی که **فهرست منابع سمینار صحیح و با DOI است**. (Confidence: High)

**حکم کلی:** Scope مصوب **نیازی به تغییر ندارد**. اما **قالب‌بندی نوآوری** باید محافظه‌کارانه بازنویسی شود و **مرکز ثقل contribution از «کنترل مشترک» به «تعمیم‌پذیری/پایداری» منتقل شود** — که هم مدفوع‌تر است و هم داخل Scope فعلی می‌گنجد. این تصمیم شماست، نه من.

---

# 2. State of the Art

| محور | وضعیت واقعی حوزه | شواهد |
|---|---|---|
| **DRL در WDN** | از ۲۰۲۰ منفجر شده. DQN رایج‌ترین (Kåge ۲۰۲۵). سه نسل: value-based (DQN/DDQN/Dueling) → actor-critic (A2C/DDPG/SAC/TD3) → policy-gradient با trust-region (TRPO/PPO) و distributional (TQC) | Negm ۲۰۲۴ (Deep), Kåge ۲۰۲۵ (Deep) |
| **Pressure Management** | مسیر تکاملی: PRV با تنظیم ثابت → NLP/MPCC مدل‌محور (Dai ۲۰۱۶/۲۰۲۱) → متاهیوریستیک (GA/PSO/DE/HHO/NSGA-II) → RL بدون‌مدل (Mosetlhe ۲۰۲۰/۲۰۲۱) → DRL (Negm، Belfadil) | Mosetlhe ۲۰۲۰ survey (Targeted) |
| **Leakage Reduction** | چارچوب IWA: ALC + pressure management + asset management + speed of repair. رابطه فشار–نشت با **FAVAD (May 1994)** و توان N1 | سمینار ص۱۳۳۱ (Deep); Negm ۲۰۲۴ |
| **PRV Control** | continuous setting رایج؛ در DRL معمولاً به‌صورت تنظیم فشار خروجی. Negm: تک‌عامل، ۸ الگوریتم. Belfadil: BDQ با گسسته‌سازی شاخه‌ای (>۱ میلیون action) | Deep ×۲ |
| **Pump/VSP Control** | جدا و بالغ‌تر از PRV: Hajgató ۲۰۲۰ (Dueling DQN)، Hu ۲۰۲۳ (E-PPO)، Ma ۲۰۲۴ (PI-MADDPG)، Pei ۲۰۲۴ (neuroevolution) | Screening/Targeted |
| **PRV + Pump مشترک** | **انجام شده.** Hu/Gao/Zhong ۲۰۲۳ با MADDPG (DRL). Monsef ۲۰۱۷ با DE. Pandurang ۲۰۲۳ با hybrid PSO | Deep + External |
| **PPO در WDN** | برای **پمپ** (Hu E-PPO)، **طراحی شبکه** (Tsiami ۲۰۲۵)، **مخزن** (Park ۲۰۲۶)، **نشت+انرژی با C-Town** (Aidan ۲۰۲۶). برای **PRV** در میان ۸ الگوریتم Negm — نه به‌عنوان برنده | Deep + External |
| **Multi-objective Reward** | **استاندارد صنعت است، نه نوآوری.** Kåge ۲۰۲۵: «automating reward function design» شکاف است چون روش فعلی «relies heavily on trial and error» | Kåge (Deep) |
| **Demand Uncertainty** | ضریب‌های ثابت روی الگو (Hu: ۰.۳/۰.۶/۰.۹ روی Net3)؛ گره‌های burst تصادفی (Negm)؛ شکست لوله تصادفی (Belfadil). **Monte Carlo نظام‌مند کم است** | Deep ×۳ |
| **PDA vs DDA** | **هر سه کار نزدیک PDA به‌کار برده‌اند.** EPANET **۲.۲** پشتیبانی native دارد (Belfadil: ۴۴ ارجاع به «2.2») | Deep ×۳ |
| **Generalization** | **ضعیف‌ترین حلقه حوزه.** Hu=۰، Belfadil=۰، Negm محدود (۶+۱۱ ارجاع). Javed ۲۰۲۵ آن را شکاف رسمی می‌داند | High confidence |
| **Robustness** | معمولاً فقط «تست روی چند سناریو»؛ آزمون آماری چندseed نایاب | Medium |
| **Sim-to-real** | شکاف اعتراف‌شده جهانی. Negm: «no test networks available in the UK» | Deep |
| **Limitations تکرارشونده** | (۱) نبود benchmark استاندارد (۲) sim-to-real (۳) پیچیدگی طراحی پاداش (۴) حساسیت hyperparameter (۵) نبود explainability (۶) بار محاسباتی | Javed+Kåge+Negm همگرا |

---

# 3. Research Corpus Overview

**۴۲ فایل، همه متن‌کاوی‌پذیر (صفر اسکن‌شده).** طبقه‌بندی:

| نوع | تعداد | نمونه‌ها |
|---|---|---|
| Journal Paper | ۱۹ | Belfadil (ASCE JWRPM), Hu (Water Supply), Hu (Systems), Dai ×۲, Samir (AEJ), Monsef (Urban Water J), Tsiami (WRM), Ledesma (IEEE TCST), Pei (JWPE), Ma (Wiley IJER), Olmuştur (**Scientific Reports**), Khalifeh (MethodsX), Moghaddam (DWT), Fakhari (JHRS), Abdy Sayyed (WRM), Mosetlhe ×۲ (Water), Bucci (Proc R Soc A) |
| Review / Systematic Review | ۵ | Mosetlhe ۲۰۲۰ survey; **Negm et al. ۲۰۲۴ (Water Research 253:121145)**; **Javed et al. ۲۰۲۵ (Water 17(13):1928)**; Negm et al. ۲۰۲۳ (IOP EES); **Kåge et al. ۲۰۲۵ (Frontiers in Water, ۱۲ مارس ۲۰۲۵, DOI 10.3389/frwa.2025.1537868)** |
| Thesis / Dissertation | ۷ | **Negm ۲۰۲۴ (PhD, Lancaster, ۳۵۸ص)**; Mosetlhe ۲۰۲۱; Puer Liu ۲۰۲۲ (MSc, Alberta); Salaorni ۲۰۲۲ (MSc, Politecnico di Milano); ۳ پایان‌نامه فارسی (مهدوی/شهید بهشتی، اسدی/شهید مدنی آذربایجان، +۱) |
| Conference Paper | ۸ | Berardi ۲۰۱۹ (E3S/EENVIRO); Stătescu ۲۰۲۴ (IOP MSE); Zaman ۲۰۲۳ (**IEEE HONET**); Negm Q-learning; Nicolini ۲۰۱۱; Ledesma ۲۰۲۰ (IFAC); فرشیدخواه ۱۳۹۸ (کنگره ملی عمران، شیراز); Hu ۲۰۲۰ (MBE) |
| Policy/Government Report | ۱ | **مرکز پژوهش‌های مجلس، مسلسل ۲۰۸۹۰، مرداد ۱۴۰۴** |

# 5. Closest Prior Works

## PW-1 — Negm (2024), PhD Thesis, Lancaster University 🔴 **نزدیک‌ترین**

*Ahmed Mohamed Abdelkader Atia Negm, "Water Pressure Optimisation for Leakage Management Using Deep Reinforcement Learning", January 2024, ۳۵۸ص, با همکاری Designed Network Solutions Ltd.* **[Deep, Full-text]**

- **مسئله:** کاهش نشت پس‌زمینه و burst از طریق مدیریت فشار با PRV
- **الگوریتم:** ۸ الگوریتم DRL با **Stable-Baselines3**، معماری Nature-CNN (۳۲/۶۴/۶۴) + ۲ لایه FC
- **State/Action:** فضای عمل **پیوسته** (فرض صریح)؛ observation از شبکه
- **Reward:** `R = scale₁·Σ(v_before − v_after) + scale₂·Σ[(Q_lb − Q_la)/Q_lb]` + جریمه‌های `P_Leak`/`P_Solved`. حدود فشار **۱۰–۷۰ متر (OFWAT DG2, UK)**. **وزن‌ها با آزمون تکراری و نمودار سه‌بعدی trade-off و مشورت با شرکت آب انتخاب شده**
- **مدل نشت:** emitter coefficient + leakage exponent در EPANET، توزیع‌شده بر طول لوله
- **هیدرولیک:** **PDA** (۶۹ ارجاع)، رابط **epynet**
- **شبکه‌ها:** **Jowitt & Xu** (benchmark، دارای مخزن/PRV) + **SZ08** (شبکه واقعی Northumbrian Water)
- **Baseline:** DE، PSO، **Nelder-Mead**
- **عدم‌قطعیت:** گره‌های burst تصادفی
- **نتایج:** benchmark: ۶۵.۲٪↓ نشت پس‌زمینه، ۵۸.۴۶٪↓ burst + ۵۶۵۰kg CO₂. **واقعی: «negligible» و ۵.۷۹٪ + ۱۹۹۹kg**
- **برنده‌ها:** TQC (Jowitt & Xu) / TRPO (SZ08) / A2C (burst, ۴۲.۱۵). SAC=۲۱.۸۲، DDPG=۱۸.۵۴ (بدترین)
- **محاسبات:** <۰.۴s در سطح DMA؛ **~۱۰s برای کل سیستم — «real-time control is slightly out of the scope of DRL using regular processors»**
- **فرض بحرانی:** *"pressure valves are able to process precise settings provided by the agent whereas in practice some control errors can be expected"*
- **انجام نداده:** پمپ/VSP؛ تعمیم cross-network نظام‌مند؛ عدم‌قطعیت **تقاضا** (فقط burst)
- **شباهت:** ≈۸۵٪ از پشته روش‌شناختی پروژه
- **تفاوت واقعی:** افزودن پمپ/VSP + عدم‌قطعیت تقاضا + تمرکز بر تعمیم. **تفاوت علمی است، نه implementation detail — اما incremental و پیش‌بینی‌شده**

## PW-2 — Hu, Gao & Zhong (2023), _Water Supply_ 23(7):2833 🔴 **تهدید اصلی نوآوری اول**

DOI 10.2166/ws.2023.163، Harbin Institute of Technology، Open Access CC BY 4.0 **[Deep]**

- **کنترل مشترک پمپ + PRV** با **MADDPG**، صریحاً «to address the uncertainty of water demand in WDNs»
- *"the status of the pumps and control valve settings of the **PRVs**"*؛ *"The pumps and valves **work together**"*
- **PDA (۸)، emitter (۱۰)، uncertainty (۱۲)**
- Action space PRV از «minimum pressure requirement of consumers and the valve inlet pressure» با **۱۰۰۰ اپیزود تعامل تصادفی** تعیین شده
- Baseline: **GA، PSO، DE** — MADDPG سریع‌تر و بهتر
- یافته: **«water loss dominates the scheduling process»**؛ راه‌حل‌ها به **الگوی مصرف** وابسته‌اند نه تعرفه انرژی
- **انجام نداده:** `generaliz`=۰؛ بدون هدف نوسان/smoothness؛ multi-agent نه single-agent
- **تفاوت باقی‌مانده با پروژه شما:** single-agent PPO (on-policy) در برابر MADDPG (multi-agent off-policy) + افزودن جریمه نوسان + مطالعه تعمیم. **این تفاوت علمی است ولی باریک**

## PW-3 — Belfadil et al. (2023), ASCE JWRPM 🟠

*Anas Belfadil; David Modesto; Jordi Meseguer; Bernat Joseph-Duran; David Saporta; Jose Antonio Martin Hernandez*, DOI 10.1061/JWRMD5.WRENG-6108 **[Deep]**

- **BDQ / BDQF**، **EPANET 2.2** (۴۴ ارجاع)، **PDA (۹)**
- **>۱ میلیون action در هر گام**؛ **۱۰ شبکه واقعی** (Hidralia + Aigües de Barcelona)
- **۲۶٪ بهبود فشار میانگین**؛ عدم‌قطعیت: شکست لوله تصادفی، عدم‌قطعیت تقاضا، آلودگی

- **`generaliz`=۰**
- **این کار «چارچوب یکپارچه DRL↔EPANET» را قبلاً تثبیت کرده** → شکاف پنجم سمینار را رد می‌کند

## PW-4 — Hu et al. (2023), _Systems_ 11(2):56 🟠 **مهم‌ترین Counter-Evidence برای PPO**

- **PPO و E-PPO** برای پمپ، Net3، عدم‌قطعیت با ضرایب ۰.۳/۰.۶/۰.۹
- **«E-PPO can learn suboptimal scheduling policies»** (اعتراف نویسندگان)
- **GA بهینه بود** (به‌نقل Negm ص۹۲۷)؛ ترتیب: GA > E-PPO > PPO > DE > PSO
- مزیت DRL: **۰.۴۲s** استنتاج بدون بازآموزی

## PW-5 — Monsef, Naghashzadegan, **Farmani**, Jamali (2017) 🟡

دانشگاه گیلان + دانشگاه Exeter. **PRV + VSP مشترک** با DE: **۴۱.۷۲٪↓ نشت پس‌زمینه، ۲۸.۴٪↓ انرژی**. محدودیت: الگوی تقاضای ثابت. **این نشان می‌دهد «کنترل هماهنگ PRV+پمپ» از ۲۰۱۷ در ادبیات هست — نوآوری پروژه فقط در «با DRL/PPO» است.**

# 8. Proposal/Seminar Claims Review

طبق **§19 Conflict Protocol**:

## ادعا ۱ 🔴 **بحرانی** — «چارچوب PPO+EPANET وجود ندارد»

- **Proposal §۱:** «به‌طور خاص، چارچوب منسجمی که الگوریتم PPO را با محیط‌های مبتنی بر EPANET ادغام کند، وجود ندارد… کاربرد آن در مدیریت بلادرنگ… هنوز به‌خوبی بررسی نشده است»
- **Evidence:** Negm ۲۰۲۴ محیط Python↔EPANET ساخت و PPO+RecPPO را اجرا کرد؛ Belfadil ۲۰۲۳ «DRL-EPANET» را در ASCE منتشر کرد؛ Hu ۲۰۲۳ PPO/E-PPO روی Net3؛ Tsiami ۲۰۲۵ PPO+EPANET. **همه در Corpus خودتان یا ضمیمه ۱ خودتان.**
- **تعارض:** ادعا با ضمیمه ۱ همان سند در تناقض مستقیم است
- **نوع:** **Scientific error + internal inconsistency** (نه wording)
- **شدت:** **بالا** — قابل رد در جلسه دفاع با یک ارجاع
- **Minimum Correction:** جمله را به «چارچوب‌های PPO+EPANET وجود دارند اما تک‌عملگری‌اند؛ کنترل هم‌زمان PRV و VSP با یک عامل PPO و ارزیابی تعمیم‌پذیری آن کمتر بررسی شده» تغییر دهید
- **بدون تغییر Scope؟** ✅ بله
- **نیاز به تصمیم استاد؟** توصیه می‌شود (اصلاح متن Proposal مصوب)

## ادعا ۲ 🔴 **بحرانی** — «۳۲ میلیارد مترمکعب (Guo et al., 2013)»

- **Evidence:** Liemberger & Wyatt (در Corpus): **«346 million cubic meters per day or 126 billion cubic meters per year»**، «**the 2006 estimates were extremely conservative**»، «aggregate NRW is **30%** of water system input volumes»، «USD **39 billion** per year». و Guo et al. ۲۰۱۳ (طبق فهرست منابع سمینار خودتان) = *"Two-dimensional pipe leakage through a line crack"*, J Zhejiang Univ-SCIENCE A 14(5):371-376 — **مقاله فیزیک نشت، نه منبع آمار جهانی**
- **نوع:** **Scientific error (عدد) + citation misattribution**
- **شدت:** **بالا** (جمله دوم Proposal است)
- **Minimum Correction:** «۱۲۶ میلیارد مترمکعب در سال، معادل ۳۰٪ حجم ورودی سیستم‌های آبرسانی جهان (Liemberger & Wyatt, 2019)»
- **Scope:** بدون تغییر ✅

## ادعا ۳ 🟠 — «قاعده ۱٪»

- **Proposal §۱:** «شواهد تجربی نشان می‌دهد که هر ۱٪ کاهش در هدررفت آب، منجر به ۱٪ کاهش در هزینه کل تولید و حفظ ۱٪ از منابع آب آشامیدنی موجود می‌شود»
- **Evidence:** **هیچ ارجاعی ندارد.** رابطه ۱:۱ خطی بین کاهش نشت و کاهش «هزینه کل تولید» با اقتصاد آب سازگار نیست (هزینه‌های ثابت/سرمایه‌ای مقیاس نمی‌خورند)
- **نوع:** **Unsupported claim** — احتمالاً بین «۱٪ کاهش نشت ≈ ۱٪ کاهش حجم تولید» و «هزینه کل» اشتباه شده
- **شدت:** متوسط
- **Minimum Correction:** حذف یا جایگزینی با ارجاع اقتصادی معتبر (Corpus شما «مروری بر روش‌های تحلیل اقتصادی نشت» دارد)

## ادعا ۴ 🔴 **بحرانی (روش‌شناختی)** — توجیه PPO با on-policy بودن

- **سمینار ص۸۴–۸۵ (شکاف چهارم):** «از آنجا که PPO یک الگوریتم on-policy است… این ویژگی امکان انطباق تدریجی سیاست با تغییرات محیط و کاهش حساسیت به ناهنجاری‌های گذرا را فراهم می‌کند و می‌تواند گامی مؤثر در جهت کاهش شکاف میان شبیه‌سازی و واقعیت تلقی شود»
- **Evidence — این استنتاج نامعتبر است:** on-policy بودن یک ویژگی **تخمین‌گر گرادیان سیاست در زمان آموزش** است، نه سازوکار انطباق در زمان استقرار. یک سیاست PPO منجمدشده **هیچ انطباقی ندارد**. کاهش شکاف sim-to-real از domain randomization، robust/adversarial training، system identification و safe RL می‌آید. علاوه‌براین on-policy **کم‌بازده‌تر از نظر نمونه** است (نقطه‌ضعف برای شبیه‌ساز گران) و برای انطباق آنلاین در سیستم ایمنی‌محور **بدتر** است چون exploration با سیاست جاری در محیط واقعی لازم دارد
- **نوع:** **Methodological weakness / non-sequitur در استدلال** — نه ایراد بر خودِ انتخاب PPO
- **شدت:** **بالا** (ممکن است هدف سؤال داور شود)
- **Minimum Correction:** توجیه PPO را روی زمینه‌های قابل دفاع بگذارید: clipped surrogate → به‌روزرسانی محدود و پایدار؛ پشتیبانی بومی از فضای عمل پیوسته چندبعدی؛ **تحمل بازه پهن learning-rate (شاهد: Park et al. ۲۰۲۶: 1e-5..3e-4 در برابر 1e-3 برای DQN)؛ افت ۱۲٪ در برابر ۲۸٪ تحت نویز**. و sim-to-real را جداگانه با **randomization سناریوهای تقاضا** (که Proposal از قبل دارد) آدرس دهید
- **Scope:** بدون تغییر ✅ — **PPO تغییر نمی‌کند، فقط استدلالش**

## ادعا ۵ 🟠 — شکاف پنجم سمینار: «چارچوب یکپارچه… نوآورانه است»

رد می‌شود با Belfadil ۲۰۲۳ (چارچوب DRL-EPANET، ASCE، ۱۰ شبکه واقعی) و Negm ۲۰۲۴ (محیط اختصاصی). **نوع:** overstated novelty. **شدت:** متوسط-بالا. **اصلاح:** «یکپارچه‌سازی برای کنترل هم‌زمان چند نوع عملگر» به‌جای «یکپارچه‌سازی».

## ادعا ۶ 🟠 — نوآوری دوم: پاداش چندهدفه

Negm پاداش چندهدفه با **مطالعه حساسیت وزن و نمودار سه‌بعدی trade-off** ساخته. Kåge ۲۰۲۵: طراحی پاداش چندهدفه **رویه رایج** است و «trial and error» نقطه‌ضعف حوزه است. **اصلاح:** نوآوری را از «طراحی پاداش چندهدفه» به «افزودن term نوسان/smoothness + مطالعه ablation وزن‌ها» محدود کنید.

تو اکنون وارد Phase 1.5-B پروژه می‌شوی:

Evidence Completion & Deep Verification

Phase 1.5 قبلی یک مرور اولیه و نسبتاً عمیق از Research Corpus، Proposal، Seminar و بخشی از ادبیات خارجی انجام داده است.

اما گزارش قبلی صریحاً نشان داد که Review هنوز کامل و نهایی نیست.

بنابراین این Phase را «ادامه و تکمیل همان Review» در نظر بگیر، نه یک Literature Review جدید از صفر.

==================================================
تنظیم سطح تلاش و Reasoning
==================================================

این Phase برای تصمیم‌های علمی مهم است.

از بالاترین سطح Effort / Reasoning موجود استفاده کن:

Maximum / Highest

سرعت اولویت اصلی نیست.

تمرکز اصلی:

- Verification
- Counter-Evidence
- رفع ابهام
- تکمیل شواهد
- بررسی نزدیک‌ترین رقبا
- بررسی ادبیات جدید
- کنترل ادعاهای Novelty
- و کاهش عدم‌قطعیت

Maximum Effort فقط برای کیفیت تحلیل است.

هیچ اجازه‌ای برای تغییر فایل، تغییر Scope، تغییر Methodology یا Implementation ایجاد نمی‌کند.

==================================================
اصل اصلی
==================================================

مرور قبلی را دوباره از صفر انجام نده.

همان گزارش Phase 1.5 را به‌عنوان working baseline در نظر بگیر و فقط:

- شکاف‌های evidence
- ادعاهای مشکوک
- findings با confidence پایین/متوسط
- موارد Pending Verification
- مقالات جدید تأییدنشده
- نزدیک‌ترین prior works
- و ادعاهای Novelty

را تکمیل و راستی‌آزمایی کن.

اگر یک finding قبلی به اندازه کافی مستند و تأییدشده است، دوباره‌کاری نکن.

==================================================
1. ابتدا گزارش قبلی را مبنا قرار بده
==================================================

گزارش Phase 1.5 قبلی را بررسی کن و تمام موارد زیر را استخراج کن:

- Pending Verification
- NV
- Confidence = Low
- Confidence = Medium
- External source not fully verified
- Claims based on limited evidence
- Novelty claims needing stronger evidence
- Contradictions requiring resolution
- Proposal/Seminar claims flagged as problematic
- Critical methodological uncertainties

یک فهرست «Evidence Gap List» بساز.

در این مرحله هنوز هیچ فایلی را تغییر نده.

==================================================
2. اولویت‌بندی Evidence Gaps
==================================================

Evidence Gapها را بر اساس اهمیت دسته‌بندی کن:

### Priority 1 — Critical
مواردی که ممکن است:

- Novelty را رد کنند.
- Research Question را تحت تأثیر قرار دهند.
- Methodology را تغییر دهند.
- یک ادعای اصلی Proposal را غلط نشان دهند.
- یک prior work بسیار نزدیک را آشکار کنند.

### Priority 2 — Important
مواردی که ممکن است:

- طراحی آزمایش
- Baseline
- Evaluation
- Reward
- State
- Action
- Generalization

را تحت تأثیر قرار دهند.

### Priority 3 — Supporting
مواردی که بیشتر برای کامل‌تر شدن Literature Review هستند و فعلاً تصمیم اصلی پروژه را تغییر نمی‌دهند.

ابتدا Priority 1 را بررسی کن.

==================================================
3. Verify Near-Competitors First
==================================================

اول از همه نزدیک‌ترین prior workها را Verify کن.

به‌خصوص کارهایی که مستقیماً روی این موارد اثر دارند:

- PRV + Pump + DRL
- PPO + EPANET
- Pressure Management + DRL
- Leakage Reduction + DRL
- Demand Uncertainty + DRL
- Joint Actuator Control
- Generalization / Transferability

برای هر near-competitor مشخص کن:

- منبع اصلی چیست؟
- publication type چیست؟
- سال
- عنوان دقیق
- نویسندگان
- DOI یا شناسه معتبر در صورت وجود
- روش
- Algorithm
- PRV
- Pump/VSP
- Reward
- Demand uncertainty
- PDA/DDA
- Network
- Evaluation
- دقیقاً چه چیزی انجام داده‌اند؟
- دقیقاً چه چیزی انجام نداده‌اند؟

هر نکته مهم را تا حد امکان با primary source تأیید کن.

==================================================
4. Novelty Verification
==================================================

تمام ادعاهای Novelty قبلی را دوباره بررسی کن.

Novelty را جزءبه‌جزء بررسی کن:

- Problem
- Method
- Algorithm
- PRV
- Pump/VSP
- Joint actuator control
- Reward
- Demand uncertainty
- Generalization
- Experimental protocol
- Combination of components

برای هر مورد:

### Status
یکی از این موارد:

- Already Established
- Strong Overlap
- Partial Overlap
- Potentially Differentiated
- Uncertain

### Evidence
منابع مشخص.

### Closest Prior Work
نزدیک‌ترین نمونه.

### Remaining Uncertainty
چه چیزی هنوز قطعی نیست.

### Confidence
High / Medium / Low

قانون مهم:

هرگز از «پیدا نشدن مقاله در جست‌وجوی فعلی» نتیجه نگیر که «هیچ‌کس قبلاً انجام نداده است».

عبارت درست در چنین شرایطی:

«در جست‌وجوی انجام‌شده، مورد تأییدشده‌ای پیدا نشد.»

نه:

«این کار قبلاً انجام نشده است.»

==================================================
5. Verify 2025–2026 Literature
==================================================

در Review قبلی چند منبع جدید 2025–2026 پیدا شد که به دلیل:

- 429
- محدودیت API
- محدودیت ابزار
- یا عدم استخراج کامل

به‌طور کامل Verification نشده بودند.

فقط همین منابع و موارد مشابه را دوباره بررسی کن.

اولویت:

1. آبجکت/عنوان دقیق
2. صفحه رسمی ناشر
3. DOI / شناسه معتبر
4. Abstract
5. در صورت امکان Full Text

اگر یک API مثل Semantic Scholar rate-limited است:

- چند بار بی‌فایده retry نکن.
- منبع دیگری را امتحان کن.
- در صورت نیاز از وب/ناشر/DOI/صفحه رسمی استفاده کن.
- اگر باز هم قابل تأیید نیست، آن را Pending Verification نگه دار.

هیچ نتیجه‌ای را فقط به دلیل وجود عنوان یا abstract ناقص قطعی نکن.

==================================================
6. Verify Proposal و Seminar Claims
==================================================

فقط ادعاهای مهمی را که در Review قبلی مشکل‌دار شناخته شده‌اند دوباره Verify کن.

به‌خصوص:

- ادعای «عدم وجود چارچوب PPO + EPANET»
- ادعای Novelty
- آمار جهانی NRW
- ادعاهای مربوط به PPO و sim-to-real
- ادعاهای مربوط به PDA/DDA
- ادعای «یکپارچه‌سازی» یا «novel framework»
- هر citation مشکوک
- هر مرجع اشتباه یا ناقص

برای هر مورد:

1. متن ادعا
2. منبع ادعا
3. Evidence
4. وضعیت:
   - Correct
   - Needs Clarification
   - Scientifically Problematic
   - Misattributed
   - Outdated
5. Minimum Scientifically Valid Correction

فعلاً هیچ سندی را اصلاح نکن.

==================================================
7. Verify Counter-Evidence
==================================================

برای یافته‌های مهم قبلی، بررسی کن Counter-Evidence واقعاً از منبع می‌آید یا فقط inference بوده.

به‌خصوص:

- benchmark generalization
- network dependence
- PPO performance
- DRL vs classical optimization
- reward design
- PDA vs DDA
- leakage modelling
- continuous action
- reward hacking

هرجا inference بوده، صریحاً آن را به‌عنوان Inference نگه دار.

Inference را به‌عنوان Direct Evidence ارائه نکن.

==================================================
8. Verify PDA / DDA Evidence
==================================================

فقط شواهد مورد استفاده در Review قبلی را بررسی و تکمیل کن.

بررسی کن:

- مطالعات نزدیک دقیقاً چه نوع hydraulic analysis دارند.
- PDA چگونه پیاده شده.
- DDA چه فرضی دارد.
- leakage model چیست.
- emitter یا FAVAD/N1 چگونه استفاده شده.
- آیا leakage و unmet demand قابل تفکیک هستند.
- آیا DDA می‌تواند reward پروژه را مخدوش کند.
- آیا PDA انتخاب روش‌شناختی مهمی برای مسئله است یا فقط یک implementation choice.

فعلاً PDA یا DDA را انتخاب نکن.

==================================================
9. Verify Reward Evidence
==================================================

تمرکز فقط روی شواهد مربوط به:

- pressure penalty
- leakage objective
- energy
- smoothness
- constraint violation
- multi-objective reward
- reward weights
- scaling
- normalization
- sensitivity
- reward hacking

بررسی کن:

- آیا multi-objective reward واقعاً contribution محسوب می‌شود؟
- آیا weighting دستی روش متداول است؟
- چه روش‌های دیگری در literature وجود دارد؟
- آیا منابعی برای sensitivity / ablation وجود دارند؟
- آیا rewardهای قبلی failure mode ایجاد کرده‌اند؟

فعلاً Reward نهایی را طراحی نکن.

==================================================
10. Verify State / Action Evidence
==================================================

فقط شواهد مرتبط با:

### State
- pressure
- flow
- demand
- tank
- actuator
- historical observations
- time features

### Action
- PRV
- pump speed
- VSP
- continuous/discrete
- single-agent/multi-agent

را بررسی کن.

تمرکز روی این باشد که:

- چه انتخاب‌هایی رایج‌اند؟
- چرا؟
- چه محدودیت‌هایی دارند؟
- چه انتخاب‌هایی برای پروژه ما plausible هستند؟

اما هنوز State یا Action نهایی نکن.

==================================================
11. Verify Baseline Evidence
==================================================

بررسی کن که baselineهای مناسب در کارهای نزدیک چه بوده‌اند:

- Fixed control
- Rule-based
- GA
- PSO
- DE
- MPC
- Classical optimization
- RL alternatives
- PPO alternatives

و مشخص کن:

- کدام baselineها ضعیف‌اند.
- کدام baselineها معتبرترند.
- کدام baseline برای thesis من از نظر علمی قابل دفاع‌تر است.

اما Baseline نهایی را انتخاب نکن.

==================================================
12. Verify Demand Uncertainty and Generalization
==================================================

بررسی کن:

### Demand Uncertainty
- historical
- stochastic
- synthetic
- Monte Carlo
- perturbation
- distribution shift
- scenario-based

### Generalization
- unseen demand
- unseen topology
- multiple networks
- cross-network transfer
- robustness
- transfer learning

مشخص کن:

- کدام‌ها قبلاً انجام شده‌اند.
- کدام‌ها محدودیت دارند.
- کجا Evidence قوی است.
- کجا gap واقعی‌تر است.

فعلاً طراحی uncertainty protocol نکن.

==================================================
13. Verify Network Evidence
==================================================

نام شبکه‌هایی که در Review قبلی مطرح شدند را فقط در حد Evidence بررسی کن.

برای هر شبکه مهم:

- منبع اصلی
- اندازه
- topology
- pump
- valve
- tank/reservoir
- EPANET
- leakage suitability
- literature usage
- computational complexity
- relevance

فعلاً هیچ شبکه‌ای را انتخاب نکن.

==================================================
14. جدول Evidence Status

---

### 1. Cyriac & Chacko
- **Title:** "Deep Reinforcement Learning for Pressure Optimization in Water Distribution Networks with Multiple Pumping Stations"
- **Authors:** Unni Cyriac (first; ORCID 0009-0001-2318-4282, authenticated), Sibi Chacko (additional) — both Heriot-Watt Univ., United Arab Emirates
- **Journal:** "Journal of Water Resources Planning and Management"
- **Published:** July 1, 2026 (2026-07-01)
- **DOI:** 10.1061/jwrmd5.wreng-7303
- **Abstract:** None included in the record. Type: journal-article.

---

### 2. León-Celi et al.
- **Title:** "A Methodology for the Optimization of Flow Rate Injection to Looped Water Distribution Networks through Multiple"… — the title closes with a reference to pumping stations.
- **Authors:** Christian León-Celi (first), Pedro Iglesias-Rey (ORCID 0000-0001-8300-3255), F. Martínez-Solano (0000-0002-8140-5960) — all Universitat Politècnica de Valencia, Spain; Daniel Mora-Melia (0000-0002-6191-7299) — Universidad de Talca, Chile
- **Journal:** "Water"
- **Published:** December 6, 2016 (2016-12-06)
- **DOI:** 10.3390/w8120575
- **Abstract (summary):** The authors argue a network works best when demands are met with minimum energy while the required minimum pressure is preserved. They propose optimizing injected flow rate using "the setpoint curve concept," assessing the flow and pressure head each pumping station must deliver at lowest power draw. Two variants are offered: a discrete method testing a finite set of station combinations, and a continuous one where "Hooke–Jeeves and Nelder–Mead algorithms are used." Hydraulics and the objective function are computed with "EPANET and its Toolkit," and two case studies are discussed.

---

### 3. Joo, Jeong & Kang
- **Title:** "Deep Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Objective Real-Time Pump Operation in Rainwater Pumping Stations"
- **Authors:** Jin-Gul Joo (first; Dongshin University, Naju), In-Seon Jeong (Chonnam National University, Gwangju), Seung-Ho Kang (Dongshin University, Naju) — Republic of Korea
- **Journal:** "Water"
- **Published:** November 26, 2024 (2024-11-26)
- **DOI:** 10.3390/w16233398
- **Abstract (summary):** Rainwater pumping stations near cities or farmland limit flooding by switching on pumps of differing capacity according to live inflow, but the authors state that "rule-based pump operations that monitor only basin water levels" are frequently inadequate. Besides holding peak water level down, operators want fewer on/off cycles, since "Reducing pump switch frequency lowers the likelihood of mechanical failure" and cuts maintenance cost. Their deep reinforcement learning controller uses only currently observable variables — rainfall, inflow, storage volume, basin level, outflow. Training rainfall of varied return periods and durations was synthesized with the Huff method, and SWMM was set up to represent the Gasan station in Geumcheon-gu, Seoul; results were benchmarked against the station's existing rule-based scheme.

---

### 4. Li et al. (preprint)
- **Title:** "Optimization of DMAs design and cooperative pressure reducing valves and pumping stations to achieve leakage control"… — continues with an energy-saving strategy for water distribution networks.
- **Authors:** HongYan Li (first), Wentao Shi, Zifeng Chang, Feng Zhang, Jianguo Cui (all Taiyuan University of Technology); Xulong Lu (Institute of Architectural Engineering Design CNNC Co.7 Research and Design Institute Co); Libo Mao (Shanxi Dadi Environment Investment Holdings Co)
- **Journal/container:** None listed; record type is "posted-content" (preprint)
- **Published:** June 4, 2024 (2024-06-04)
- **DOI:** 10.21203/rs.3.rs-4399025/v1
- **Abstract (summary):** Addressing leakage and energy use in urban water distribution networks, the paper offers a new workflow for creating district metered areas and managing pressure. Step one pairs NSGA-III with spectral clustering — weighing partition cost, operational difficulty, post-partition water quality, and supply capacity — and uses multicriteria decision making to select layouts and boundary pipes. Step two applies NSGA-II to site valves and flow meters on those boundary pipes, judged on equipment cost, water quality, and leakage reduction. Finally, pressure reducing valves at DMA inlets are co-scheduled with fixed- and variable-speed pumps via a genetic algorithm. Tested on the SH town network, the approach reportedly cut leakage and pumping energy and also "improve the water quality of networks."

**Abstract (summarized — too long to quote in full):** The authors note that data assimilation matters for uses spanning climate and weather prediction through to route planning for self-driving vehicles, and that the ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) depends on linear updates that reduce ensemble variance. They argue recent deep learning work has been largely supervised, leaving open the question of how well such models generalize to situations they were not trained on. Their proposal applies reinforcement learning to correct model states from complete or incomplete observations, tested on the chaotic Lorenz '63 system, where the agent aims "to minimize the root-mean-squared error between the observations and corresponding forecast states." Because the action policy is stochastic, repeated sampling yields an ensemble of assimilated realizations in a Monte Carlo framework. Reported outcomes compare favorably with the EnKF, and the agent can also handle non-Gaussian data, which they describe as "a significant limitation of the EnKF."

content.content:
**Note on the comparison baseline:** The page describes version 2.2 as an advance over the first community release (v2.1), not v2.0 — it says 2.2 offers "some major improvements over the first community release of EPANET." No details about EPANET 2.0 appear on this page.

**Yes, pressure-dependent demand is listed as a 2.2 feature.** The only text on the page about demand models is this bullet:

> "the ability to use **pressure dependent demands** in hydraulic analyses"

The page does not use the acronym "PDA," nor does it describe the specific demand-model formulations or parameters.

**Other highlights listed for 2.2:**

- A complete API for reading and writing model parameters: "includes a full set of functions to set and retrieve values for **all parameters** contained in a network model"
- Model creation without an input file: "networks can be built **programmatically**; completely from function calls instead of from an input file"
- Parallel analysis: "multiple projects can be analyzed in parallel in a **thread-safe** manner"
- Numerical/accounting improvements: "more robust results with regard to **hydraulic convergence**, low/zero flow conditions, and water quality **mass balance**"
- Speed: "**faster run times** for single period hydraulic analyses"
- Compatibility with the EPA-released graphical interface: "the updated DLL will work with the current GUI released by US EPA"

For reference, later releases in the 2.3 line added further capabilities (positional control valves, FAVAD pipe leakage, controls enable/disable, flow balance reporting, expanded pressure units, Tag editing, and a C# binding), with several 2.3.x patches fixing units-conversion and toolkit-setter bugs.
